items.title: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown.
METHODS: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.
RESULTS: A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group.
CONCLUSIONS: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

items.title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan in ERBB2-Low Advanced Breast Cancer: The HORIZON-Breast06 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) has demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in a global phase 1 trial involving heavily pretreated patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2)-low metastatic breast cancer.
OBJECTIVE: To compare trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, randomized, multicenter phase 3 trial was conducted at 73 hospitals across China. Eligible patients were females aged 18 to 75 years with centrally confirmed ERBB2-low (immunohistochemistry [IHC] 1+ or IHC 2+/in-situ hybridization [ISH]-negative) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received 1 or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor-positive disease. Enrollment began on June 30, 2023, and ended on August 20, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the final analysis for progression-free survival in the current study was March 20, 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab rezetecan (6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks; n = 277) or physician's choice of chemotherapy (n = 274).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and the overall population.
RESULTS: Between June 30, 2023, and August 20, 2025, a total of 551 patients were randomized, with a mean (SD) age of 54.9 (9.9) years. At the data cutoff (March 20, 2026), trastuzumab rezetecan significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with chemotherapy in the chemotherapy-naive patients (median, 16.6 [95% CI, 14.0-19.4] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-7.0] months; hazard ratio, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.19-0.33]; P < .001) and the overall population (median, 16.4 [95% CI, 14.0-16.8] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-6.9] months; hazard ratio, 0.27 [95% CI, 0.21-0.34]; P < .001). The benefit was consistent in hormone receptor-negative disease (median progression-free survival: 16.5 vs 6.8 months; hazard ratio, 0.34, [95% CI, 0.22-0.54]) and hormone receptor-positive disease (median progression-free survival: 16.4 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.18-0.33]). Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events occurred in 84.1% of patients (232/276) with trastuzumab rezetecan and 67.9% (184/271) with chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (180 [65.2%] vs 147 [54.2%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Trastuzumab rezetecan provided significant progression-free survival benefit over physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer, with benefit observed across all key subgroups. It exhibited the potential as a new treatment option with a distinct safety profile in this setting.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05814354.

items.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.
METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.
FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.
INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. items.title: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing.
RESULTS: Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, -11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs -5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, -5.3 [95% CI, -8.9 to -1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, -12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, -6.2 [95% CI, -10.2 to -2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 76%, 85%, and 73% of participants in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively; most events (99.7%) were mild or moderate. Overall, most participants were deemed ready for discharge within 2 hours post dose (85% for 8 mg and 78% for 12 mg).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms. Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively.

items.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.
METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

items.title: Tarlatamab-Durvalumab Maintenance for Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear.
METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here.
RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab.
CONCLUSIONS: Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

items.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.
METHODS: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.
RESULTS: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

items.title: Preoperative Intranasal Oxytocin and Probable Acute Stress Disorder After Traumatic Fracture Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Acute stress disorder (ASD) is a common and debilitating psychological sequela following traumatic fracture surgery, adversely affecting recovery and predicting chronic posttraumatic stress disorder. Effective pharmacological prevention strategies are currently lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a single preoperative dose of intranasal oxytocin for the prevention of screening-positive probable ASD in patients undergoing traumatic fracture surgery.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted at the General Hospital of Western Theater Command in China. From April 2024 to April 2025, adult patients scheduled for traumatic fracture surgery were enrolled and randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either receive intranasal oxytocin, 40 IU, or an equivalent volume of intranasal saline placebo 10 minutes before the induction of anesthesia.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of a first screening-positive probable ASD within 3 days postoperatively, defined by a Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SAS-RQ) score of 40 or higher. Key secondary outcomes included the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and salivary malondialdehyde, cortisol, and superoxide dismutase levels.
RESULTS: A total of 328 patients were randomized (164 to the saline group and 164 to the oxytocin group) and included in the intention-to-treat analysis. The median (IQR) age of all participants was 50 (34-57) years; 210 participants (64.0%) were male, and 118 participants (36.0%) were female. The 3-day cumulative incidence of screening-positive probable ASD was 26 of 164 (15.9%) in the oxytocin group vs 50 of 164 (30.5%) in the saline group (risk difference, -14.6 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI, -23.5 to -5.5 pp; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.34-0.79). In the prespecified Cox model, preoperative oxytocin was associated with a lower hazard of a positive screening result during follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.27-0.75). Exploratory analyses suggested improved psychological outcomes and directionally consistent alterations in stress biomarker trajectories. No serious adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative intranasal oxytocin is associated with a lower cumulative incidence of probable ASD after traumatic fracture surgery. These findings suggest that intranasal oxytocin may represent a feasible perioperative preventive strategy; however, these exploratory mechanistic insights and long-term safety profile warrant further investigation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry Identifier: ChiCTR2400082612.

items.title: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.
METHODS: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.
RESULTS: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group.
CONCLUSIONS: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

items.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C-Mutated NSCLC.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.
METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.
RESULTS: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; P<0.001). The median overall survival was 17.7 months with divarasib and 12.0 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for death, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.78; P<0.001). Of the 328 patients who could be evaluated for response, a confirmed response occurred in 58.4% in the divarasib group and in 32.3% in the control group. The median duration of response was 11.9 months with divarasib and 6.9 months with control treatment. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

items.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC.
METHODS: MASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete.
FINDINGS: Between Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24). There were two serious adverse events attributable to SBRT; grade 2 small bowel obstruction and grade 3 pancreatitis.
INTERPRETATION: In patients with high-risk, localised PDAC, the addition of SBRT to chemotherapy was associated with significantly reduced locoregional recurrence without a significant increase in toxicity and warrants further investigation in larger studies.

items.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial.
items.abstract: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) is overexpressed in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and was recently identified as a potential therapeutic target to overcome resistance to programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death ligand 1 (PDL1) blockade. We investigated the safety and efficacy of GDF-15 blockade in an exploratory, stratified, placebo-controlled, single-blinded, nonrandomized phase 2a trial (GDFATHER-NEO). Thirty-one cisplatin-ineligible or cisplatin-refusing patients with newly diagnosed MIBC (clinical T2-T4aN0M0) were stratified by tumor stage and PDL1 combined positive score (CPS) and allocated sequentially to receive three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab (N, 480 mg 4-weekly) plus the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab (V, 20 mg kg-1 4-weekly; n = 16) or placebo (P, n = 15), followed by radical cystectomy or repeat transurethral resection of the bladder tumor. Locally assessed pathologic complete response (pCR, ypT0N0/x) and Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1-based radiographic response served as dual primary endpoints. pCR was 33% (5 of 15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 12-62%) in patients receiving N + V versus 8% (1 of 13, 95% CI 0-36%) for N + P; major pathologic response was 60% (95% CI 32-84%) versus 23% (95% CI 5-54%), and radiographic overall response rate was 60% (95% CI 32-84%) versus 15% (95% CI 2-45%), respectively. Responses to N + V were associated with higher baseline densities of total and proliferating (Ki-67+) CD8+ T cells, but independent of CPS and baseline GDF-15 levels in serum and tumor. There were no treatment-related discontinuations or treatment-related delays to surgery; grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (13%) and three (20%) patients treated with N + V or N + P, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of visugromab in MIBC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06059547 .

items.abstract: Camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) drives mutated KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell responses that correlated with disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with mKRAS pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. In the phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial, patients with stage I-III KRAS-mutated PDAC without recurrence within 6 months of standard therapy were randomized 2:1 to camupepimut (n = 96) or standard-of-care/observation (n = 48). Stratification balanced nodal status. The primary DFS endpoint was not met (median 23.8 versus 21.2 months; HR 0.85, P = 0.5329). However, prespecified and exploratory analyses were informative. A numerical DFS advantage at 6 months of 14.0% (75.7% versus 61.7%; HR 0.55, P = 0.0557) corresponded to camupepimut dosing. Post hoc multivariate Cox regression analysis of DFS indicated an improved outcome for camupepimut (adjusted HR 0.47, P = 0.0086), a worse outcome for stage III disease (adjusted HR 2.29, P = 0.0127), an elevated baseline CA19-9 (adjusted HR 3.16, P < 0.0001) and baseline circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) positivity (adjusted HR 5.99, P < 0.0001). Prespecified subgroup analyses addressing prognostic and predictive factors suggested DFS benefit for camupepimut (ctDNA negative: HR 0.51, P = 0.0280; no prior radiation: HR 0.59, P = 0.0221). Exploratory analysis demonstrated that ex vivo mKRAS-specific T cell responses were robust (98.9%, 89/90) and associated with antigen spreading (86.7%, 13/15). In camupepimut-treated patients, mKRAS-specific T cell response >9.17-fold over baseline (82.2%, 74/90) correlated with improved DFS (HR 0.22, P < 0.0001), with the median DFS not reached versus 6.08 months for above and below 9.17-fold, respectively. Camupepimut safety was similar to observation, with grade ≥3 adverse events in 10.4% (10/96) versus 14.6% (7/48), and few serious AEs (6.3%, 6/96 versus 8.3%, 4/48; reflecting progression/surgical complication). These efficacy and immunogenicity signals will inform a refined strategy for a confirmatory phase 3 trial. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05726864 .

items.title: Durvalumab, Tremelimumab, and Enfortumab Vedotin in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown.
METHODS: In this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival.
RESULTS: In total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; P<0.001); estimated overall survival at 24 months was 78.4% and 69.4%, respectively (hazard ratio for death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.83; P = 0.003). Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 60.1% (95% CI, 53.2 to 66.2) with durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (hazard ratio for an event or death vs. control, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 71.1% of patients in the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 30.7%), in 79.5% of those in the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 44.5%), and in 50.2% of those in the control group.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus three cycles of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin resulted in significantly better event-free survival outcomes than surgery alone. Perioperative durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin led to significantly better overall survival outcomes than surgery alone. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause were noted in more than half the patients in the durvalumab groups. (Funded by AstraZeneca; VOLGA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04960709; EudraCT number, 2020-005452-38.).

items.title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial.
items.abstract: Nivolumab plus relatlimab is approved for advanced melanoma based on the RELATIVITY-047 trial; however, long-term data are needed. Here, we report data from RELATIVITY-047 with the longest follow-up at present. In this phase 2-3, double-blind trial, patients with metastatic/unresectable melanoma were randomized 1:1 to nivolumab 480 mg plus relatlimab 160 mg (n = 355) or nivolumab 480 mg (n = 359) intravenously every 4 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review. Secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), response, and safety. Additional post-hoc analyses such as melanoma-specific survival (MSS), and exploratory biomarker analyses are also reported. This analysis shows clear separation in survival curves with the largest absolute differences to date in PFS, OS, and MSS. In this prespecified 5-year analysis, with a minimum follow-up of 57.3 months, nivolumab plus relatlimab demonstrated continued clinically significant benefit versus nivolumab for PFS (hazard ratio = 0.77; 95% confidence interval: 0.65-0.92), OS (hazard ratio = 0.78; 95% confidence interval: 0.64-0.95), and MSS (hazard ratio = 0.71; 95% confidence interval: 0.57-0.88). The safety profile remained consistent with prior reports. Among biomarker-evaluable patients in the programmed death ligand 1 ≥1% subgroup, analyses revealed an association between worse outcomes with nivolumab and high peripheral or tumor lymphocyte activation gene 3 (LAG-3)+ CD8 cell levels. The addition of relatlimab to nivolumab was associated with a lower prevalence of primary resistance than nivolumab alone. These data support the hypothesis that relatlimab can overcome LAG-3-mediated resistance to nivolumab and provides evidence for differential efficacy patterns observed across biomarker subgroups linked to primary versus acquired resistance states. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03470922.
